argument_summary: The admissible record does not support unconditional certification on the present packet, but it does support a narrower position: certification is policy-compliant if and only if the current release documentation is the governing artifact, reflects the current evaluation batch, and explicitly discloses the clinical-trial intake regression that is 1.1 percentage points below the warning threshold. Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall launch readiness, while the policy and model-card guidance allow launch with disclosed current limitations. The prior approval and informal monitoring note are contextual only and should not be treated as substitutes for current-release documentation or approved mitigation.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit concern. The governance question can be answered on the admissible record by narrowing the certification basis to current-documentation compliance.
claims_about_policy: The policy standard in the record is conditional, not absolute: certification may proceed when current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed, or when those weaknesses are covered by approved mitigation. On this record, prior approval of the model family and the informal monitoring comment do not satisfy that requirement. The cleanest policy reading is therefore caveated compliance tied to current-release disclosure, not stale-approval compliance.
concessions: The present admissible record does not show that the required current-release disclosure or approved mitigation already exists.
The clinical-trial intake slice is weaker than in the prior approved release and is below the warning threshold in the current release.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is not a reviewed mitigation or risk acceptance artifact.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No private or side-channel material is relied on as public support.
